name: Do vanity replacements require building permits in the Salt Lake Valley?

mainEntity.name: Do vanity replacements require building permits in the Salt Lake Valley?

acceptedAnswer.text: You generally do not need a building permit to swap an existing vanity in place using identical plumbing connections. However, if your replacement project involves opening walls to relocate drain and vent stacks, altering electrical wiring, or reconfiguring structural framing, local Salt Lake Valley building jurisdictions often require trade permits. Working with a licensed general contractor ensures that any mechanical, electrical, or plumbing updates completed during the installation comply with local residential codes and pass necessary inspections.
acceptedAnswer.description: Simple direct swaps using existing plumbing do not require permits. If you move plumbing lines, add electrical circuits, or open interior walls, local permits are generally required.
